steps.seen: SPLIT RESULT, measured two ways. (a) WORK-ORDER CARD drag: a ghost DOES follow the cursor - a clone of the sidebar card reparented to <body>, reading 'S8685-12876 / 1 line - 1h Est. / Pamill Paving / 713 / AC Alicia Campbell'. It carries the HOURS but names the line COUNT, not the line's name. (b) DRILL-DOWN LINE drag: no element carrying the dragged line's name ('Diagnose - Oil Leak') was found anywhere outside the sidebar in a whole-tree hunt at two points mid-drag, and none is visible in the mid-drag screenshot evidence/ghost-22.png. The 24 and 21 text matches found were pre-existing blocks already on the calendar; the cursor moved +369,+138 between samples and NO match moved with it. Harness ruled out: the same pointer events that produced no ghost DID produce the drop-target highlight and DID complete the drop, so the drag mechanism was working.

steps.step: 3 releasing outside any valid cell creates nothing

steps.step: NOTE on what would still explain (b)
steps.seen: If the line drag used the browser's NATIVE HTML5 drag image, that image is drawn by the compositor, is absent from the DOM and absent from screenshots - so neither check could see it. Against that: the CARD drag on the same page renders its mirror as a real DOM node, so this app draws DOM mirrors. Recorded as an observation, NOT called a defect.
